title: New Medical Trial Aims to Stop Alzheimer’s Before Symptoms Begin
subtitle: Researchers are testing an experimental drug on healthy individuals to see if it can prevent memory loss.

summary.en: A new international study called PrevenTRON is testing a drug on people who do not yet have Alzheimer’s symptoms. The trial focuses on individuals aged 55 to 80 who are at a higher risk of developing the disease. Researchers are using a blood test to identify a specific protein that predicts future memory problems. The drug, trontinemab, works by clearing toxic proteins from the brain. Experts hope this shift toward prevention will help millions of people in the future.
summary.zh: 一項名為「PrevenTRON」的新國際研究正在測試一種針對尚未出現阿茲海默症症狀者的藥物。該試驗聚焦於五十五至八十歲、罹患該疾病風險較高的人群。研究人員利用血液檢查來識別一種可預測未來記憶問題的特定蛋白質。藥物「trontinemab」的作用機制是清除腦中的毒性蛋白質。專家希望這種轉向預防的策略，未來能造福數百萬人。

paragraphs.en: For many years, medical research into Alzheimer’s disease has focused on finding treatments for patients who are already showing signs of memory loss. However, a new international study is changing this approach by looking at whether the disease can be stopped before it even starts. According to The Guardian Health, a new clinical trial called PrevenTRON is now recruiting healthy middle-aged people to test an experimental drug that may prevent dementia from developing.
paragraphs.zh: 多年來，阿茲海默症的醫學研究一直聚焦於為已經出現記憶力衰退跡象的患者尋找治療方法。然而，一項新的國際研究正透過探討是否能在疾病發生前就將其阻斷，從而改變這種研究方向。根據《衛報健康》（The Guardian Health）報導，一項名為「PrevenTRON」的新臨床試驗目前正在招募健康的中年人，以測試一種可能預防失智症發生的實驗性藥物。

paragraphs.en: Alzheimer’s disease is a serious condition that affects millions of people globally. It is estimated that the disease begins to develop inside the brain up to 10 years before a person starts to notice any memory problems. Currently, the condition affects about one in 14 people over the age of 65, and this number increases to one in six for those over 80. Because the disease often causes brain cells to die over time, scientists are eager to find ways to intervene at an earlier stage.
paragraphs.zh: 阿茲海默症是一種影響全球數百萬人的嚴重疾病。據估計，該疾病在患者開始察覺任何記憶問題前，可能已在腦部發展長達十年之久。目前，六十五歲以上的人口中，約有十四分之一的人患有此病，而八十歲以上的人口中，這一比例則上升至六分之一。由於該疾病常導致腦細胞隨時間死亡，科學家們迫切希望找到在更早期階段進行干預的方法。

paragraphs.en: The PrevenTRON study is looking for 1,600 participants between the ages of 55 and 80 from around the world. In the UK, the Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS foundation trust is leading the recruitment process. The first step for potential participants is a screening to ensure they do not currently have any memory issues. If they pass this stage, they will have a blood test to check for a specific biomarker called p-tau217. A biomarker is a biological sign in the body that can help doctors predict the development of a disease. Previous research suggests that high levels of p-tau217 are linked to a 78% chance of developing cognitive problems within 10 years.
paragraphs.zh: 「PrevenTRON」研究計畫在全球尋求一千六百名年齡介於五十五歲至八十歲之間的參與者。在英國，薩里與邊界國民保健署信託基金會（Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS foundation trust）正主導招募流程。潛在參與者的第一步是接受篩檢，以確保他們目前沒有任何記憶方面的問題。若通過此階段，他們將進行血液檢查，以檢測一種稱為「p-tau217」的特定生物標記。生物標記是指體內有助於醫師預測疾病發展的生物徵兆。先前的研究顯示，高濃度的 p-tau217 與十年內出現認知障礙的風險有百分之七十八的關聯。

paragraphs.en: The drug being tested is called trontinemab, which was created by the Swiss pharmaceutical company Roche. This medicine works by attacking amyloid plaques. These are toxic proteins that build up in the brain and eventually kill brain cells. Early research on patients who already had early-stage Alzheimer’s showed that the drug was very effective at clearing these plaques. In fact, the drug removed these harmful proteins in nine out of 10 people within 28 weeks. Now, researchers want to see if the same drug can stop the disease from developing in people who are currently healthy but at risk.
paragraphs.zh: 此次測試的藥物名為「trontinemab」，由瑞士藥廠羅氏（Roche）研發。這種藥物的作用機制是攻擊類澱粉蛋白斑塊。這些斑塊是堆積在腦部並最終導致腦細胞死亡的毒性蛋白質。針對已患有早期阿茲海默症患者的初步研究顯示，該藥物在清除這些斑塊方面非常有效。事實上，該藥物在二十八週內清除了十分之九受試者體內的這些有害蛋白質。現在，研究人員希望觀察同樣的藥物是否能阻止目前健康但具有風險的人群發展出該疾病。

paragraphs.en: Professor Ramin Nilforooshan, who is the chief investigator for the trial, explained that this study represents a major shift in how scientists think about the disease. He noted that for decades, the focus was only on treating patients after symptoms appeared. By moving the focus to prevention, researchers hope to stop the damage before it becomes permanent. At least 15 hospitals and clinics across the UK are expected to join the study by the end of the year. The trial will last between four and six years, during which time participants will be randomly chosen to receive either the drug or a placebo—a substance with no medicine in it used for comparison.
paragraphs.zh: 擔任該試驗首席研究員的拉敏·尼爾福魯山教授（Professor Ramin Nilforooshan）解釋說，這項研究代表科學家對該疾病的看法出現了重大轉變。他指出，數十年來，研究重點僅在於患者出現症狀後的治療。透過將重心轉向預防，研究人員希望在損害成為永久性之前將其阻止。預計到今年年底，英國各地至少有十五家醫院和診所將加入這項研究。試驗將持續四至六年，期間參與者將被隨機分配接受藥物或安慰劑——一種不含藥物成分、用於對照比較的物質。

paragraphs.en: Despite the excitement surrounding this new study, experts are being careful not to promise too much too soon. Professor Nilforooshan spoke to the Telegraph about the need for caution, noting that the treatment is still experimental. He explained that the trial is not magic and that researchers must wait to see the results to determine if the drug actually works as expected. Because the trial is still in its early stages, it remains a scientific investigation rather than a proven cure.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管這項新研究令人振奮，但專家們仍謹慎行事，避免過早做出過多承諾。尼爾福魯山教授在接受《每日電訊報》（The Telegraph）採訪時談到了謹慎的必要性，並指出該治療方法仍處於實驗階段。他解釋說，這項試驗並非魔法，研究人員必須等待結果出爐，才能確定該藥物是否如預期般有效。由於試驗仍處於早期階段，它目前仍屬於科學調查，而非已證實的療法。

paragraphs.en: This study is a significant step forward in understanding how to protect brain health. If the trial is successful, it could change the lives of millions of people who are at risk of developing dementia. For now, the medical community is watching the progress of the PrevenTRON study closely. Those who are interested in participating in the trial can contact the research team at the Surrey and Borders Partnership for more information about the screening process.
paragraphs.zh: 這項研究是了解如何保護腦部健康的重要進展。如果試驗成功，它可能改變數百萬面臨失智症風險者的生活。目前，醫學界正密切關注「PrevenTRON」研究的進展。有意參與試驗者可聯繫薩里與邊界國民保健署的研究團隊，以獲取更多關於篩檢流程的資訊。

keyTerms.definitionEn: Removing unwanted things from a place.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作形容詞（清楚的），這裡作動詞清除之意。文中：Early research on patients who already had early-stage Alzheimer’s showed that the drug was very effective at clearing these plaques.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To accumulate or increase in quantity over time.
keyTerms.noteZh: 由動詞與介詞組成，意思與單字原意不同。文中：These are toxic proteins that build up in the brain and eventually kill brain cells.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To successfully complete a test or reach a required standard.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作動詞（經過/傳遞），這裡指通過篩選階段。文中：If they pass this stage, they will have a blood test to check for a specific biomarker called p-tau217.

quiz.question: What is the specific requirement for a potential participant to be tested for the p-tau217 biomarker?

options.A: They must be between 65 and 80 years old.
options.B: They must successfully pass a screening to confirm they have no current memory issues.
options.C: They must be diagnosed with early-stage Alzheimer’s disease.
options.D: They must be a patient at the Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS trust.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，參與者在進行 p-tau217 生物標記檢測前，必須先通過篩選以確保目前沒有記憶問題。選項 A 錯誤，因為招募年齡範圍是 55 至 80 歲，而非 65 歲起。選項 C 錯誤，因為該研究招募的是「健康」且尚未出現症狀的人。選項 D 錯誤，因為雖然該機構負責招募，但並未要求參與者必須是該機構的現有病患。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the development of Alzheimer’s disease based on the text?

options.A: It is impossible to detect the disease before symptoms appear.
options.B: The disease is caused primarily by the presence of p-tau217 in the blood.
options.C: Brain damage caused by Alzheimer’s is likely irreversible once symptoms become noticeable.
options.D: The drug trontinemab is only effective for people over the age of 80.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章第五段提到，研究人員希望透過預防性治療在損害變得「永久性（permanent）」之前介入，這暗示了一旦症狀出現，腦部損傷可能已無法逆轉。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章提到 p-tau217 等生物標記可用於預測疾病。選項 B 錯誤，p-tau217 是疾病發展的「指標」，而非導致疾病的「原因」。選項 D 錯誤，研究招募對象是 55 至 80 歲，並未指出藥物僅對 80 歲以上者有效。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the word 'progress' mean in the context of the PrevenTRON study?

options.A: A physical movement toward a destination.
options.B: The development or advancement of an ongoing process.
options.C: A formal meeting to discuss research findings.
options.D: The act of increasing the number of participants.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在文中，「watching the progress of the study」是指觀察該研究進行的過程與發展狀況，屬於抽象意義的進展。選項 A 錯誤，因為這不是指實體的移動。選項 C 錯誤，文中並未提到有任何會議。選項 D 錯誤，進展（progress）涵蓋研究的整體執行與結果，而不僅僅是招募人數的增加。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of this article?

options.A: Roche has successfully cured Alzheimer’s disease using trontinemab.
options.B: The UK government is changing how they fund medical research for the elderly.
options.C: Medical researchers are shifting focus toward early prevention of Alzheimer’s disease.
options.D: People over 55 should be worried about their risk of developing dementia.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章的核心主旨是介紹醫學界如何從「症狀出現後治療」轉向「早期預防」，並透過 PrevenTRON 研究來驗證此概念。選項 A 錯誤，因為藥物尚在實驗階段，並非已證實的療法。選項 B 錯誤，文章未提及政府資金政策的改變。選項 D 錯誤，雖提及風險，但文章重點在於研究的科學意義與預防潛力，而非製造恐慌。
